column3: NASB follows the critical text (“the world”); “as not using it as their own” is rendered “as though they did not make full use of it.”
NASB renders “without concern” as “free from concern” and “cares for” as “is concerned about.”
NASB renders “cares for” as “is concerned about.”
NASB follows the critical text, adding “his interests” and treating the unmarried woman and the virgin as two subjects.
NASB adds “to promote” and renders the last phrase as “to secure undistracted devotion to the Lord.”
NASB adds “daughter,” taking “his virgin” as a daughter; the meaning is uncertain.
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “daughter.”

NASB follows the critical text without “by the law”; “has died” is rendered “is dead.”
